blocks.content: When we count a node as double-black, it contributes twice to the black depth along that path.

blocks.alt: Double Black Node Contributes Twice the Black Depth

blocks.content: However, double-black isn't a valid color for a node. So, this problem needs to be addressed.
Marking a node as double-black precisely indicates where there's a deficit of black in the tree.
Without this marker, tracking this imbalance within the larger structure of the tree would be challenging. Think of it as a temporary marker for our reference.
If the parent is red, it will now be a black node.

blocks.alt: If Parent of Double Black Node is Red, Make it Black

blocks.content: If the parent is black, it will now be a new double black node.

blocks.alt: Black Parent as a New Double Black Node

blocks.content: However, we cannot transfer a double black from a parent to its child.
Let's look at some of the cases that arise when removing a double black node.
